messages:
Micah: heads-up — canary of runtime build 2.3.1 with new PTX emitter landed in us-west-2 ~08:12UTC and we're seeing a regression on H100 (SM90) nodes. ~8% of running jobs hit PTX JIT errors and crash. :warning:
Anya: logs? short snippet pls
Micah: dmesg from one host:
```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00.0: PTX JIT compile failed: ptx version 90 not supported by driver
[ 1234.568034] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x10de)
```
Zara: that error screams "emitter produced PTX targeting sm90 with PTX version newer than driver supports" — which fits the new emitter change. Any `nvidia-smi`/driver info?
Devon: on one affected node:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q | grep -E "Driver Version|CUDA Version"
Driver Version                     : 535.86
CUDA Version                       : 12.1
```
Micah: yep, driver is 535.86. New PTX requires driver >= 540 (canary notes said optional), looks like our fleet mix has older kernel modules on some AZs.
Anya: deploy-bot shows canary rolled to 20% in us-west-2 at 08:12:21:
```
[deploy-bot] rollout: runtime/2.3.1 -> 20% (us-west-2) by ci/canary
[deploy-bot] change: ptx-emitter: enable-sm90-ptxv
```
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2025-1782 (priority P1) — affected capacity: 120 GPUs, approx 3% of active cluster capacity.
Zara: immediate mitigation options?
Devon: options listed from canary runbook:
- rollback runtime to 2.3.0 (fast, avoids driver mismatch)
- or force driver upgrade to min 540 across affected nodes (slower; kernel rebuilds on some AMIs)
- temporary scheduler anti-affinity for nodes reporting JIT failures
Micah: rollback looks fastest. Rolling back now to stop ongoing job failures.
Anya: can we avoid recurrence? Long-term we need to ensure runtime emitter only produces PTX that is backward compatible with our lowest supported driver OR we set a driver-min policy for regions.
Zara: agree. Also need improved canary checks: detect PTX JIT failures in canary and auto-abort rollouts. Right now our canary metric is just success/failure of unit tests — doesn't catch runtime JIT compile errors.
Devon: I'm patching the autoscaler to mark nodes with >3 JIT errors as unschedulable. Pushing flag to staging.
Micah: cost impact: because we rolled back and rescheduled ~25 interrupted jobs, estimate ~120 GPU-hours wasted and some spot churn. Finance FYI: extra spot spend ~ $4.2k.
Anya: customer impact? early pager for a hosted customer saw degraded throughput for ~17 minutes. Notifying support to open tickets for impacted tenants.
Zara: next steps (action items):
1) rollback confirmed by deploy-bot (Micah) — done at 08:21UTC
2) add PTX JIT failure detector to canary suite (Anya) — PR opened
3) decide driver minimum policy per region and update infra AMI build (Devon) — meeting scheduled 10:00UTC
4) add scheduler safeguard to drain/cordon nodes that hit repeated JIT failures (Devon) — in progress
5) postmortem draft (Zara) — I'll start, include cost and customers
Micah: rolling logs + host list attached to INC-2025-1782. If anyone has node IDs with different kernel module versions please paste here.
Devon: found 3 AMIs in us-west-2 with older kernel pkg that prevented driver 540 from loading cleanly — pushing fixes to AMI bake pipeline.
Anya: TL;DR: new emitter produced PTX targeting newer PTX version; some nodes' drivers are too old -> JIT fails -> jobs crash. Rollback done, mitigations in motion.
Zara: postmortem will include timeline, cost estimate, and checklist to block new emitter changes unless driver-min policy enforced. Also include auto-abort for canaries that produce kernel/dmesg errors.
Micah: thanks all. tagging @oncall for follow-up. :thumbsup:
